recommendation: Reject the original draft. Authorise the three costed actions subject to the stated sales, instructor and booking conditions. Withhold approval of the full annual budget: the management plan still forecasts a EUR19,745.83 operating loss. Review monthly results before making further commitments.
risks: The forecast is an estimate, not a register of signed contracts. January and February delivery depend on an opening pipeline and existing supplier bookings that the case does not confirm.

Internal allocations assume the senior instructor is already paid within the EUR2,500 delivery department salary and can teach the selected programmes. The extra allowance, training and two-day monthly reserve are budgeted. If all allocations need external cover, the forecast loss becomes EUR70,503.43.
Anna must accept the proposed independent contract. The 40% recovery rate is a management assumption and does not duplicate the portfolio already covered by Ella or the existing programme calendar.

Pooled enquiry conversion does not prove demand at EUR600 per seat. Linda must screen interest in the premium course, allocate the existing campaigns to the new dates and confirm at least eight prepaid seats.
Fractional days are expected budget volumes. A dated calendar must reserve whole programme blocks and distinct assistants. September requires three assistants simultaneously for two days.
The residual corporate mix and travel cost are estimates. Historical sales revenue and recorded programme counts do not provide a reconciled customer-level delivery schedule.

decisions.decision: Offer Anna an independent portfolio-retention contract
decisions.timing: Negotiate in January–February. Proposed contract operates March–December. Recognise incremental sales only in delivery months.
decisions.cost: 10% total commission on the contract channel. Ordinary5% is already costed. Additional premium EUR2,170. No fixed salary after February.
decisions.effect: Recover40% of the former seasonal corporate portfolio not already covered by Part1. Adds EUR15,500 revenue, mainly March–July. Do not duplicate Ella’s portfolio.
decisions.feasibility: Anna knows these clients. Acceptance, account ownership and timely proposals are conditions. Retention rate is a management estimate.

decisions.decision: Schedule four additional Executive Blame Delegation open courses
decisions.timing: Proposed dates27–28Feb,23–24Apr,18–19Jun and10–11Dec2026. Book suppliers by11Jan,26Feb,23Apr and15Oct respectively. February requires confirmed six-week notice; otherwise move it into March and revise the monthly budget.
decisions.cost: EUR1,000 January setup plus all trainer, room, materials and commission costs. At external fees the extra events cost EUR13,840 before internal allocation. Existing annual marketing EUR52,500 remains.
decisions.effect: Serve unserved forecast demand:14,13,13,15 seats at EUR600. Adds55 seats and EUR33,000 revenue.
decisions.feasibility: Linda owns segmentation, promotion and prepaid bookings. Allocate existing campaigns to the new dates. Require at least eight prepaid seats, review price-specific demand, and use rooms of20. No conversion-rate increase is assumed.
